from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The Gaussian distribution has a characteristic bell shape.", "It is defined by mean and variance.", "Mean determines the center of the curve."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction & Prerequisite Intuition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        circle = Circle(color="#FF00FF", radius=0.5)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24).next_to(circle, UP)
        circle_group = VGroup(circle, label_a)
        
        square = Square(color="#00FFFF", side_length=0.8)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24).next_to(square, UP)
        square_group = VGroup(square, label_b)
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=circle.get_right(), end=square.get_left(), color="#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(circle), Write(label_a))
        self.place_at_grid(circle_group, "C2")
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(square), Write(label_b))
        self.place_at_grid(square_group, "C5")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(label_a.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), label_b.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Summing independent Gaussians results in another Gaussian.",
            "New mean is the sum of original means.",
            "New variance is the sum of original variances."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Addition Principle (Intuitive Phase)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        gauss1 = Ellipse(width=1.5, height=1.0, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        gauss2 = Ellipse(width=1.5, height=1.0, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        label1 = Text("N(μ₁, σ₁²)", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF")
        label2 = Text("N(μ₂, σ₂²)", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        
        union_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=3, height=2.5, width=4)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(gauss1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(gauss2, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "B5")
        self.play(Create(gauss1), Write(label1), Create(gauss2), Write(label2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(union_box, "B2", "E5")
        self.play(Create(union_box))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeOut(gauss1), FadeOut(label1), FadeOut(gauss2), FadeOut(label2))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Adding two independent variables corresponds to convolution.", 
                         "Two narrow bell curves merge into one wider.", 
                         "Wider curve reflects increased uncertainty."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the 'Convolution' Effect", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        func1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#00FFFF")
        func2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#00FFFF")
        result = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.exp(-x**2 / 2), x_range=[-4, 4], color="#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(func1, "A1", "C3")
        self.place_in_area(func2, "A4", "C6")
        self.play(Create(func1), Create(func2))
        self.play(func1.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5), func2.animate.shift(LEFT * 1.5), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(result, "D1", "F6")
        self.play(FadeOut(func1), FadeOut(func2), Create(result))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        label = Text("Wider Variance", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "D5")
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Key Takeaways & Real-World Application", 
                          ["Gaussians are closed under addition.", 
                           "Errors accumulate but retain the Gaussian family.", 
                           "Essential for combining sensor data."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display bullet point list #FFFFFF of takeaways.
        takeaways = VGroup(

            Text("Gaussian Family Persistence", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF"),

        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(takeaways, 'A1', 'D3')
        self.play(Write(takeaways))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        conclusion = Text("Real-world Reliability", font_size=32, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, 'F3')
        self.play(FadeIn(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian

sections.title: Introduction & Prerequisite Intuition
sections.content: Briefly define a Gaussian (Normal) distribution via its 'bell curve' shape. Establish the prerequisite: A random variable is defined by its mean (μ, the center) and variance (σ², the spread).
sections.example: Imagine a robot arm moving. The error in its X-position is a Gaussian bell curve. If we have two independent error sources, what happens when we combine them?

sections.title: The Addition Principle (Intuitive Phase)
sections.content: Introduce the core concept: If X ~ N(μ₁, σ₁²) and Y ~ N(μ₂, σ₂²) are independent, then their sum S = X + Y is also a Gaussian distribution. Visually illustrate how the means add up (μ_sum = μ₁ + μ₂) and the variances add up (σ²_sum = σ₁² + σ₂²).
sections.example: A cat jumps from a shelf. Component 1: The 'intended jump distance' (μ₁, σ₁²). Component 2: The 'wind gust displacement' (μ₂, σ₂²). The total landing spot is the sum of two bells.

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Convolution' Effect
sections.content: Show an animation of two bell curves sliding across each other. Explain that the addition of two independent variables is mathematically equivalent to the 'convolution' of their probability density functions (PDFs).
sections.example: Visual animation: Two distinct narrow blue bell curves merge into one wider, shorter purple bell curve. This represents the increased uncertainty (wider variance) after combining two independent errors.

sections.title: Key Takeaways & Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize that Gaussian distributions are 'closed' under addition. This is why the Normal distribution is so powerful in nature—errors and noises accumulate but retain the same 'family' of distribution.
sections.example: In sensor fusion, a self-driving car combines data from a GPS sensor (Gaussian error A) and a LiDAR sensor (Gaussian error B). The resulting fused position estimate remains a Gaussian, making it easy to calculate the final confidence interval.
